title: C# Login Project · Complete and Test
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: A print server must process jobs in the order submitted. Choose a suitable data structure and explain why a stack would be unsuitable.
questions.answer: Use a queue: FIFO serves the earliest job first. A stack uses LIFO and would process the most recently added job first.

blocks.title: Your goal: a reliable demonstration system
blocks.text: Students will join registration and lookup so the program recognises existing usernames, refuses duplicates and performs login checks.

blocks.title: Validation before storage
blocks.text: Reject blank usernames, duplicates and registrations when all buckets are full. Show a meaningful reason rather than crashing.

blocks.title: Separate locating an account from checking a password
blocks.text: First use the hash table to find the username. Then compare an invented classroom demo password. These are separate operations.

blocks.title: Design the test evidence
blocks.text: Test normal, erroneous and boundary scenarios: new user, unknown user, duplicate username, collision, table full and maximum attempts.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model validation before registration
blocks.text: Add one small safeguard at a time rather than copying a completed login system.
